thread:
support-eng: FYI customer Aurora reporting major throughput drop after the 03:12 UTC deploy. Throughput ~120rps -> ~30rps, 95p latency from ~80ms -> ~450ms on /generate. Model: redwood/gptx-13b-8k:v2.1. Trace ids: trace=trc_0a9f; sample request attached. Link to customer logs: https://s3.company/aurora/logs/1760123000
maya: Thanks — do we have the deploy id? any runtime changes in the release? did we change KV cache behavior or batching defaults?
jonathan: I didn't touch runtime. Release was a modelstore/quantization push for gptx-13b v2.1. Deploy id: deploy-20260317-0312 (modelstore). No infra config changes on my end.
support-eng: reproducer (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood/gptx-13b-8k:v2.1","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256,"temperature":0.0}' -v
```
Also header: x-trace-id: trc_0a9f
lina: I'll pull perf dashboards now. @ramiro can you check autoscaling and any sudden instance churn? I'll also kick pprof on a handful of prod pods for 30s and paste top stacks.
ramiro: Autoscaler: no scale-down events at 03:12. Node counts stable. However GPU memory on the serving pool spiked ~+20% around the same time (likely KV cache growth). There are more small batches visible — average batch size fell from 8 -> 2 which could explain throughput drop.
jonathan: That matches a quant change I landed — the new kernel path changes how keys are cached and may increase per-request KV allocations until cache warms. Two mitigation options: 1) pin customer to model variant v2.0 (previous) or 2) force route Aurora to a dedicated pool with warmed cache. I can also roll back the modelstore artifact.
maya: For immediate mitigation can we add a routing rule to send aurora -> dedicated-pool-1 or to variant=v2.0? Support, what does customer want — rollback or route?
support-eng: Customer prefers minimal disruption; they'd accept a short rollback to v2.0 while we investigate. Please advise ETA.
lina: Pprof top (30s sample) from one warm node:
```
CPU: 30s
1  45.2%  kv_cache_lookup
2  23.1%  attn_kernel_slowpath
3  11.4%  token_loop
4   8.7%  memcpy
```
Observations: kv_cache_lookup and attn_kernel_slowpath dominate. Cache misses are high.
ramiro: Also seeing TLS backpressure in front proxy (queue growth) because backend latency spiked — frontend concurrency limits kicking in. Routing to a warmed pool should reduce frontend queues immediately.
jonathan: I'll prepare a quick rollback plan — revert modelstore artifact and restart the small subset of inference processes for Aurora routing (can do a canary rollback to 10% traffic then 100%). ETA ~20m to start canary, ~40m full rollback.
deploy-bot: deploy request created: rollbacks/modelstore/deploy-rollback-20260317-0312 by jonathan. CI checks passed.
support-eng: OK I'll tell Aurora to expect a short canary rollback. Please post updates here and tag when canary is up.
maya: Action list:
- jonathan: start rollback canary -> notify when 10% live
- lina: continue profiling + collect per-request cache metrics
- ramiro: monitor autoscaler and front proxy queues during canary
- support-eng: customer comms
jonathan: starting canary now. hitting endpoint with test load against variant=v2.0.
ramiro: front proxy queue length dropping as canary routes come up. early signs: p95 down from 450ms -> 120ms on canary nodes.
support-eng: customer confirmed improvement for canary traffic. Thanks team. I'll keep the incident open until full rollback completed.
maya: Once fully reverted we'll schedule a follow-up to dig into quant kernel changes and add a cache warmup step to model rollout. Good catch everyone. :thumbsup:
